passages.name: 2025年专八听力 Section A
passages.title: 讲座：工作记忆
passages.summary: 讲座介绍了什么是工作记忆：它是我们随时都能意识到的那部分意识，能储存当下的经历和少量知识，并在需要时从长时记忆中调取内容，帮助我们实现当前的目标。工作记忆容量大，有助于讲故事、写作、推理、交流和解决问题，但工作记忆的容量、持续时间和关注范围都有限。讲座最后介绍了弥补这些局限的五个策略：及时处理、重复练习、精细化和例证式思考、运用意象，以及有条理地组织并提供支持。

paras.en: Test for English Majors (2025), Grade Eight.
paras.zh: 英语专业八级考试（2025）。

w.m: n. 专业学生；主修科目

paras.en: Part One: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第一部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A: Mini-Lecture.
paras.zh: A节：微型讲座。

paras.en: In this section you will hear a mini-lecture.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到一篇微型讲座。

paras.en: You will hear the mini-lecture once only.
paras.zh: 这篇微型讲座你只能听一遍。

paras.en: While listening to the mini-lecture, complete the gap-filling task on Answer Sheet One and write no more than three words for each gap.
paras.zh: 请边听微型讲座，边完成答题纸一上的填空任务，每个空格填写的内容不超过三个单词。

paras.en: Make sure what you fill in is both grammatically and semantically acceptable.
paras.zh: 请确保所填内容在语法和语义上都恰当。

paras.en: You may use the blank sheet for note-taking.
paras.zh: 你可以用空白页记笔记。

paras.en: You have thirty seconds to preview the gap-filling task.
paras.zh: 你有三十秒的时间预览填空任务。

paras.en: Now, listen to the mini-lecture.
paras.zh: 现在，请听微型讲座。

paras.en: When it is over, you will be given three minutes to check your work.
paras.zh: 讲座结束后，你将有三分钟的时间检查答案。

paras.en: Working Memory.
paras.zh: 工作记忆。

paras.en: Good morning, everyone.
paras.zh: 大家早上好。

paras.en: Today, we’re going to talk about working memory.
paras.zh: 今天我们来讲讲工作记忆。

paras.en: OK, what is working memory?
paras.zh: 好，什么是工作记忆？

paras.en: Working memory is that part of our consciousness that we are aware of at any given time of day.
paras.zh: 工作记忆就是我们在一天中任何特定时刻都能意识到的那部分意识。

paras.en: In fact, you’re doing it right now.
paras.zh: 事实上，你此刻就正在运用它。

paras.en: It’s not something we can turn off.
paras.zh: 这可不是我们能关掉的东西。

paras.en: If you turn it off, that’s called a coma, loss of consciousness, right?
paras.zh: 要是把它关掉，那就叫昏迷，也就是失去意识，对吧？

paras.en: Now, What does our working memory contain?
paras.zh: 那么，我们的工作记忆里装着什么呢？

paras.en: First, it stores some immediate experiences and a little bit of knowledge.
paras.zh: 首先，它储存着一些当下的经历和少量知识。

paras.en: Second, it allows us to reach back into our long-term memory and pull some of that in as we need it, mixes it, processes it in light of whatever our current goal is.
paras.zh: 其次，它让我们能够回溯到长时记忆中，在需要时从中调取一部分，把它们融合起来，并根据我们当前的目标来加以处理，不管这个目标是什么。

w.m: det. 无论什么；不管什么

paras.en: Please note the current goal isn’t something like, I want to be the CEO in a big company or the top student in the class.
paras.zh: 请注意，这里说的当前目标，并不是像“我想成为大公司的首席执行官或者班上成绩最好的学生”这一类的。

paras.en: It’s not something like this.
paras.zh: 不是这样的目标。

paras.en: It’s more common.
paras.zh: 它要平常一些。

paras.en: For example, I’d like that biscuit, or I need to figure out how to get to the railway station.
paras.zh: 比如，“我想要那块饼干”，或者“我得弄清楚怎么去火车站”。

paras.en: So in a word, working memory capacity is our ability to take what we know and use it in ways that allow us to satisfy our current goal.
paras.zh: 所以，一句话，工作记忆容量就是我们把已知的东西拿来，以能满足当前目标的方式加以运用的能力。

paras.en: Now, let’s talk a bit more about working memory capacity.
paras.zh: 那么，我们再稍微多谈谈工作记忆容量。

paras.en: Research in this field has a fairly long history, and it shows that working memory capacity has the following positive effects.
paras.zh: 这一领域的研究历史相当悠久，研究表明，工作记忆容量有以下几方面的积极作用。

paras.en: First, people with high working memory capacity tend to be good storytellers.
paras.zh: 首先，工作记忆容量大的人往往很会讲故事。

paras.en: They tend to solve and do well on standardized tests, however important that is.
paras.zh: 他们往往能在标准化考试中解题、考出好成绩，不管这到底有多重要。

w.m: adv. 无论多么；不管怎样

paras.en: They are able to have high levels of writing ability.
paras.zh: 他们的写作能力能够达到很高的水平。

paras.en: They’re also able to reason at high levels.
paras.zh: 他们的推理能力也能达到很高的水平。

paras.en: Second, working memory is great because it helps us to communicate in such ways.
paras.zh: 其次，工作记忆很了不起，因为它能帮助我们像这样交流。

paras.en: We can have a conversation, and I can build a narrative around that, so I know where we’ve been and where we’re going, and how to contribute to this conversation.
paras.zh: 我们可以聊天，我能围绕聊的内容构建一条叙事线索，这样我就知道我们已经聊到了哪儿、接下来要聊到哪儿，以及该怎样为这场对话做出贡献。

paras.en: Third, it allows us to solve problems and do critical thinking.
paras.zh: 第三，它让我们能够解决问题，能够批判性地思考。

w.m: 批判性思维；批判性思考

paras.en: For example, when we are in the middle of a meeting, we can listen to somebody’s presentation, evaluate it, decide whether we like it or not, and ask follow-up questions.
paras.zh: 比如，开会开到一半时，我们能听别人做汇报，对其加以评估，判断自己喜不喜欢，再提出追问。

paras.en: All of that occurs within working memory.
paras.zh: 这一切都发生在工作记忆之中。

paras.en: Finally, our working memory also functions like this.
paras.zh: 最后，我们的工作记忆还会这样发挥作用。

paras.en: Suppose now we are shopping in the store, we often buy milk and eggs and bread, when at the same time, what we are really looking for is vegetable and pork.
paras.zh: 假设我们现在在商店里买东西，常常会买牛奶、鸡蛋和面包，而与此同时，我们真正要找的是蔬菜和猪肉。

paras.en: We need to make sure we’re getting what we’re looking for on those everyday occasions.
paras.zh: 在这些日常场合，我们得确保自己买到的就是要找的东西。

paras.en: Now, a central issue with working memory is that it’s limited.
paras.zh: 那么，工作记忆的一个核心问题是它是有限的。

paras.en: This means it’s limited in capacity, limited in duration, limited in focus.
paras.zh: 也就是说，它的容量有限、持续时间有限、关注范围也有限。

paras.en: We tend to remember about four things.
paras.zh: 我们往往能记住大约四件事。

paras.en: Suppose we can remember those four things for about 10 to 20 seconds unless we do something with it, unless we process it, unless we apply it to something, unless we talk to somebody about it.
paras.zh: 假设我们能把这四件事记住大约10到20秒，除非我们对它做点什么，除非我们加工它，除非我们把它运用到某件事上，除非我们跟别人谈论它。

paras.en: The problem that we have is that life now comes at us very quickly, and what we need to do is to take that abundant flow of experience and somehow extract meaning from it with a working memory, which is about the size of a pea.
paras.zh: 我们面临的问题是，如今生活以极快的速度向我们涌来，而我们需要做的，是接收这股丰富的经验之流，并设法用大约豌豆那么大的工作记忆从中提取意义。

w.m: n. 流；源源不断的一股

paras.en: But don’t get me wrong at this point, working memory is truly awesome.
paras.zh: 不过说到这里，可别误会我的意思，工作记忆确实非常了不起。

paras.en: Working memory makes us investigate our current experience as we move forward, and it helps us to make sense of the world around us.
paras.zh: 工作记忆让我们在前进的过程中审视当下的经历，还帮助我们理解周围的世界。

paras.en: But I repeat, it does have certain limits.
paras.zh: 但我要再说一遍，它确实存在某些局限。

paras.en: So when we think about working memory, we have to realize that this limited capacity has lots of different impacts on us.
paras.zh: 所以，我们在思考工作记忆时，必须认识到这种有限的容量会对我们产生许多不同的影响。

paras.en: Have you ever walked from one room to another and then forgotten why you’re there?
paras.zh: 你有没有过这样的经历：从一个房间走到另一个房间，然后忘了自己为什么要到那儿去？

paras.en: You do know the solution to that, right?
paras.zh: 那个问题怎么解决，你肯定知道，对吧？

paras.en: You go back to that original room.
paras.zh: 回到原来的那个房间去。

paras.en: We need to realize that working memory has a limited capacity.
paras.zh: 我们需要认识到，工作记忆的容量是有限的。

paras.en: So what I want to do now is to talk a little bit about a couple of strategies here, and these will be really important because you are now in an information era.
paras.zh: 所以，我现在想稍微讲讲这方面的几个策略，这些策略会非常重要，因为你们现在身处信息时代。

paras.en: Now the first part of this is that we need to process our existence, our life immediately.
paras.zh: 那么，这其中的第一点是，我们需要立即处理我们的存在，处理我们的生活。

paras.en: This means that we need to process what’s going on the moment it happens, not 10 minutes later, not a week later, but at the moment.
paras.zh: 也就是说，我们需要在事情发生的那一刻就处理正在发生的事，不是10分钟后，也不是一周后，而是就在那一刻。

paras.en: So during a meeting or conversation, we need to think about, well, do I agree with him?
paras.zh: 所以，在开会或交谈时，我们需要思考：嗯，我同意他的看法吗？

paras.en: What’s missing?
paras.zh: 还缺什么？

paras.en: What would I like to know now?
paras.zh: 我现在想知道什么？

paras.en: It’s a way of processing what’s going on so that we can use it later.
paras.zh: 这是一种处理当下所发生之事的方式，以便我们日后能加以利用。

paras.en: Second, we also need to repeat it.
paras.zh: 第二，我们还需要重复它。

paras.en: We need to practice.
paras.zh: 我们需要练习。

paras.en: So we need to think about it here.
paras.zh: 所以，我们需要在这里把它想一想。

paras.en: In between, we want to talk to people about it.
paras.zh: 在这期间，我们要跟别人谈论它。

paras.en: We’re going to write it down, and when you get home, pull out those notes and think about them and end up practicing over time.
paras.zh: 我们会把它写下来，等你回到家，就把那些笔记拿出来想一想，最终随着时间推移不断练习。

paras.en: The third thing is, we need to think elaboratively and we need to think illustratively.
paras.zh: 第三点是，我们要做精细化的思考，还要借助例证来思考。

w.m: adv. 以例证（或图示）说明地

paras.en: Oftentimes, we think that we have to relate new knowledge to prior knowledge.
paras.zh: 我们常常认为，必须把新知识和已有知识联系起来。

paras.en: How can we do it?
paras.zh: 那我们怎么才能做到呢？

paras.en: We can take all of our prior knowledge, or existence, and wrap it around that new knowledge and make all of these connections, and then it becomes more meaningful.
paras.zh: 我们可以把已有的所有知识，或者说我们的存在，拿来包裹住那条新知识，建立起所有这些联系，这样它就变得更有意义了。

paras.en: The fourth important strategy that I use is imagery.
paras.zh: 我用的第四个重要策略是意象。

paras.en: We are built for images.
paras.zh: 我们天生就是为图像而生的。

paras.en: We need to take advantage of that.
paras.zh: 我们需要利用这一点。

paras.en: Think about things in images, write things down that way.
paras.zh: 用图像来思考事物，也用这种方式把东西写下来。

paras.en: If you read a book, pull things up.
paras.zh: 如果读一本书，就把书里的东西调出来。

paras.en: For example, I just got through reading A Dream of the Red Chamber, and I have a perfect idea of what Lin Daiyu looks like in my mind, my own version of Lin Daiyu.
paras.zh: 比如，我刚读完《红楼梦》，林黛玉长什么样，我脑海里一清二楚，那是我自己心目中那个版本的林黛玉。

paras.en: Now, the last strategy.
paras.zh: 那么，最后一个策略。

paras.en: We humans are meaning-making machines.
paras.zh: 我们人类是制造意义的机器。

paras.en: It’s what we do.
paras.zh: 我们就是干这个的。

w.m: 这就是我们（天生）要做的事

paras.en: We try to make meaning out of everything that happens to us.
paras.zh: 我们试图从发生在自己身上的每一件事中获得意义。

paras.en: Here, organization helps.
paras.zh: 在这方面，条理化会有帮助。

paras.en: So we need to structure what we’re doing in ways that make sense.
paras.zh: 所以，我们需要用讲得通的方式把正在做的事组织起来。

paras.en: If we are providing knowledge and experience, we need to put it in some kind of order.
paras.zh: 如果我们要提供知识和经验，就需要把它们排出某种顺序。

paras.en: And we also need support.
paras.zh: 我们还需要支持。

paras.en: The support may come in asking people questions, giving them a sheet of paper that has an organizational chart on it, or has some guiding images.
paras.zh: 支持可以体现在向人们提问上，也可以是给他们一张印有组织结构图或者一些引导性图片的纸。

w.m: adj. 引导性的；指导性的

paras.en: So we need to support it.
paras.zh: 所以，我们需要为它提供支持。

paras.en: OK, to recap today’s lecture, we’ve talked about what working memory is, its functions, roles, and limitations, and the strategies to be used to offset the limitations.
paras.zh: 好，回顾一下今天的讲座：我们谈了什么是工作记忆，它的功能、作用和局限，以及用来弥补这些局限的策略。

paras.en: In our next lecture, we are going to talk about the functions of our long-term memory.
paras.zh: 下一次讲座，我们将讨论长时记忆的功能。

paras.en: Thank you.
paras.zh: 谢谢大家。

paras.en: Now you have three minutes to check your work.
paras.zh: 现在你有三分钟时间检查答案。

paras.en: This is the end of Section A, Mini-Lecture.
paras.zh: A节微型讲座到此结束。

passages.name: 2025年专八听力 Section B Part One
passages.title: 访谈：休息与工作（上）
passages.summary: 在访谈第一部分中，硅谷咨询顾问艾伦·李讲述了他写《休息》一书的缘由：多年的长期项目、多任务工作和出差让他出现了倦怠，而在研究中心休学术假的三个月里，他完成了大量工作，生活却出奇地悠闲。他指出，一个多世纪的研究表明，从长远来看，过度工作对个人、组织和生产力都有害；通信技术并不会自动让人更有效率，而一些公司已经在限制晚间电子邮件联系、缩短工作日，说明通信技术并非必然让人时时与工作保持联系。

paras.en: Section B: Interview.
paras.zh: B节：访谈。

paras.en: In this section you will hear one interview.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到一篇访谈。

paras.en: The interview will be divided into two parts.
paras.zh: 访谈将分为两个部分。

paras.en: At the end of each part, five questions will be asked about what was said.
paras.zh: 每部分结束时，将就所说的内容提出五个问题。

paras.en: Both the interview and the questions will be read once only.
paras.zh: 访谈和问题都只读一遍。

paras.en: After each question there will be a ten-second pause.
paras.zh: 每个问题之后有十秒钟的停顿。

paras.en: During the pause, you should read the four choices of A, B, C and D, and mark the best answer to each question on Answer Sheet Two.
paras.zh: 在停顿期间，你应阅读A、B、C、D四个选项，并在答题纸二上标出每道题的最佳答案。

paras.en: You have thirty seconds to preview the choices.
paras.zh: 你有三十秒钟的时间预览选项。

paras.en: Now, listen to Part One of the interview.
paras.zh: 现在，请听访谈的第一部分。

paras.en: Questions 1 to 5 are based on Part One of the interview.
paras.zh: 第1至5题基于访谈的第一部分。

paras.en: Good evening, everybody.
paras.zh: 大家晚上好。

paras.en: Today, we are delighted to have invited Allen Lee, a consultant in Silicon Valley to tell us his latest book Rest: Why You Get More Done When You Work Less.
paras.zh: 今天，我们很高兴请到了硅谷的咨询顾问艾伦·李，来给我们讲讲他的最新著作《休息：为什么工作越少，完成得越多》。

paras.en: This book is an empirical argument in favour of more limited working hours and greater understanding of the benefits of active rest as a means of raising creativity and productivity.
paras.zh: 这本书以实证论证主张：进一步限制工作时间，并让人们更充分地认识到主动休息的益处，把它作为提升创造力和生产力的一种手段。

w.m: adj. 实证的；以经验为依据的

paras.en: Well, Allen.
paras.zh: 那么，艾伦。

paras.en: Thanks.
paras.zh: 谢谢。

paras.en: I am very pleased to meet you all.
paras.zh: 很高兴见到大家。

paras.en: Allen, what made you decide to write the book?
paras.zh: 艾伦，是什么让您决定写这本书的？

paras.en: I’ve been working as a consultant in Silicon Valley for about 20 years, and a few years ago, after lots of long projects and multitasking and travel, I started to feel the classic effects of burnout.
paras.zh: 我在硅谷做咨询顾问已经有大约20年了。几年前，在经历了大量长期项目、多任务工作和出差之后，我开始出现典型的倦怠症状。

w.m: n. 多任务处理；同时做多件事

paras.en: My first response to this was to try to fit more into the day, to try to work harder.
paras.zh: 我对此的第一反应是，设法在一天里塞进更多事情，设法更努力地工作。

paras.en: But when I was away on sabbatical at the Blue Hill Research Center, I found that in the three months there I got an enormous amount of stuff done and did an awful lot of really serious thinking.
paras.zh: 但我在蓝山研究中心休学术假时发现，在那里的三个月里，我完成了大量的工作，还做了非常多真正严肃的思考。

paras.en: And whether you believe it or not, I also had what felt like an amazingly leisurely life.
paras.zh: 而且，不管你信不信，我当时过的生活还让我觉得出奇地悠闲。

w.m: adj. 悠闲的；从容不迫的

paras.en: Oh, that’s unbelievable.
paras.zh: 噢，这真让人难以置信。

paras.en: I didn’t feel the constant pressure to look busy or the stress that I had when I was consulting.
paras.zh: 我没有感到时刻要显得很忙的压力，也没有我做咨询时的那种紧张感。

w.m: adj. 持续不断的；经常的

paras.en: And it made me think that maybe we had this idea about the relationship between working hours and productivity backward.
paras.zh: 这让我想到，对于工作时间和生产力之间的关系，我们的这种看法或许恰恰弄反了。

paras.en: And we should make more time in our lives for leisure in the classic Greek sense, not playing a lot of video games.
paras.zh: 我们应该在生活中留出更多时间，用于古希腊意义上的闲暇，而不是玩一大堆电子游戏。

w.m: adj. 古典的（指古希腊罗马的）

paras.en: So, up until you wrote the book, you thought the more you worked the more productive you were?
paras.zh: 那么，在写这本书之前，您一直认为工作得越多，效率就越高？

w.m: adj. 效率高的；富有成效的

paras.en: Yes, there was a straight line going up.
paras.zh: 是的，就是一条往上走的直线。

paras.en: More hours equalled more productivity.
paras.zh: 工作时间更长，就等于生产力更高。

paras.en: This is an assumption, which is a mistake, really, that we’ve been making for a very long time.
paras.zh: 这是一个假设，说真的，也是一个错误，而我们犯这个错误已经很久很久了。

paras.en: And now there’s more than a century’s worth of research that shows overwork in the long run is bad for people and organisations and also bad for productivity.
paras.zh: 而现在，已有一个多世纪的研究表明，从长远来看，过度工作对个人和组织都有害，对生产力也有害。

paras.en: Overwork is something that can be sustained for a few weeks but after that, well, you start creating more problems than you solve.
paras.zh: 过度工作可以维持几个星期，但在那之后，嗯，你制造的问题就会比你解决的还多。

paras.en: We’re now living in a digital age where theoretically there is a great deal of flexibility in our modes of work but at the same time we’re more connected than ever to work.
paras.zh: 我们现在生活在数字时代，从理论上讲，我们的工作方式有很大的灵活性，但与此同时，我们和工作的联系也比以往任何时候都更紧密。

w.m: adv. 理论上；从理论上讲
adj. 有联系的；连接着的

paras.en: Can you foresee employers enforcing more detachment from work?
paras.zh: 您能预见雇主会强制员工更多地脱离工作吗？

w.m: v. 强制实行；强制推行

paras.en: Well, I think we have tended to be less critical and questioning of the virtues of new technologies, particularly communications technologies, than perhaps we should.
paras.zh: 嗯，我认为，对于新技术，尤其是通信技术的优点，我们往往批判和质疑得比较少，或许少于本该做到的程度。

paras.en: However, after a generation’s experience with emails, a decade’s experience with smartphones, we are discovering that these technologies do not automatically make us more productive or give us more time with our kids.
paras.zh: 然而，在经历了一代人的电子邮件使用和十年的智能手机使用之后，我们正逐渐发现，这些技术并不会自动让我们更有效率，也不会自动让我们有更多时间陪伴孩子。

w.m: adj. 效率高的；富有成效的

paras.en: Rather, they have tended to grind work down to a fine powder that spreads out right through our day.
paras.zh: 相反，它们往往把工作磨成细粉，撒满我们一整天。

paras.en: Is it possible to dial this back?
paras.zh: 有没有可能把这种情况往回调一调？

paras.en: The answer is there are companies that are already doing so.
paras.zh: 答案是，已经有公司在这样做了。

paras.en: They have been limiting email contact in the evening and reducing the length of the working day.
paras.zh: 它们一直在限制晚间的电子邮件联系，并缩短工作日的时长。

paras.en: Because you can have people doing an eight-hour day rather than a 10-hour day and still have people doing good work and being productive, I think these companies show that it is not inevitable that communications technologies have to keep us connected 24 hours every working day plus the weekend.
paras.zh: 因为你可以让员工一天工作八小时而不是十小时，同时仍能让他们把工作做好、保持高效，所以我认为，这些公司表明，通信技术并非必然要让我们在每个工作日外加周末都一天24小时与工作保持联系。

w.m: adj. 效率高的；富有成效的
adj. 必然的；不可避免的
adj. 有联系的；连接着的

paras.en: This is the end of Part One of the interview.
paras.zh: 访谈的第一部分到此结束。

paras.en: Questions 1 to 5 are based on what you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第1至5题基于你刚才听到的内容。

paras.en: Question 1: What can we learn about the man?
paras.zh: 第1题：关于这位男士，我们可以了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 2: What has finally made the man decide to write the book?
paras.zh: 第2题：最终是什么让这位男士决定写这本书的？

paras.en: Question 3: What does the man think about overwork now?
paras.zh: 第3题：这位男士现在如何看待过度工作？

paras.en: Question 4: What is the man’s view about new technologies?
paras.zh: 第4题：这位男士对新技术持什么观点？

paras.en: Question 5: What is the man’s attitude towards cutting down workload in the evening?
paras.zh: 第5题：这位男士对减少晚间工作量持什么态度？

passages.name: 2025年专八听力 Section B Part Two
passages.title: 访谈：休息与工作（下）
passages.summary: 在访谈的第二部分，艾伦·李指出，工作时长与生产率之间的关系并不像人们以为的那样清晰、呈线性，而保持更好的工作与生活平衡从长远看有很多好处。他认为休息远不只是不工作，锻炼、散步、认真投入的爱好等主动休息带来的益处最大；他还谈到了深度游戏（即严肃休闲）的价值，以及睡眠对大脑维护的重要作用。他说研究中最大的收获是彻底改变了对创造力的看法：创作生涯长久的人是先开始工作，然后才获得灵感。

paras.en: Now, listen to Part Two of the interview.
paras.zh: 现在，请听访谈的第二部分。

paras.en: Questions 6 to 10 are based on Part Two of the interview.
paras.zh: 第6至10题基于访谈的第二部分。

paras.en: Historically there have been very different working cultures in different places.
paras.zh: 从历史上看，不同地方的工作文化一直差别很大。

paras.en: Some have longer holidays and shorter working weeks, while others are just the opposite.
paras.zh: 有些地方假期更长、每周工作时间更短，而另一些地方恰恰相反。

paras.en: What do you think?
paras.zh: 您怎么看？

paras.en: Well, when you look at the statistics on the relationship between working hours and productivity in the world, one of the striking things you find is that it’s not as clear and linear a relationship as you think.
paras.zh: 嗯，你去看看全世界工作时长和生产率之间关系的统计数据，就会发现其中一个惊人之处：这种关系并不像你以为的那么清晰、那么线性。

paras.en: Countries like Mexico have longer working weeks and longer working years than some European countries, but they have lower productivity rates.
paras.zh: 像墨西哥这样的国家，每周的工作时间和每年的工作时间都比一些欧洲国家长，但生产率却更低。

paras.en: But the idea that it’s important to maintain better work-life balance turns out in the long run to have a lot going for it.
paras.zh: 但事实证明，从长远来看，保持更好的工作与生活平衡很重要这一理念有很多可取之处。

w.h: have a lot going for it
w.m: 有很多优点；大有可取之处

paras.en: You say in your book, rest can be defined in wider terms than that...
paras.zh: 您在书里说，休息可以从比这更宽泛的意义上来定义……

paras.en: Yes, we often think of rest as a negative term defined by absence of work, but it’s really much more than that.
paras.zh: 是的，我们常常把休息看作一个消极的概念，用没有工作来界定它，但它其实远不止于此。

paras.en: The counterintuitive discovery is that many of the most restorative kinds of rest are actually active.
paras.zh: 一个违反直觉的发现是，很多最能让人恢复精力的休息方式其实都是主动的。

w.m: adj. 有恢复作用的；恢复精力的

paras.en: Things like exercise or walks or serious, engaging hobbies do more for you than sitting on the couch watching television.
paras.zh: 像锻炼、散步，或者需要认真投入、让人沉浸其中的爱好，对你的好处都比坐在沙发上看电视大。

w.m: adj. 引人入胜的；吸引人的

paras.en: The kind of rest, like watching TV, playing video games, certainly has its place but active rest delivers the greatest benefits.
paras.zh: 像看电视、玩电子游戏这类休息当然有它的用处，但主动休息带来的益处最大。

paras.en: It also provides occasion for creative reflection.
paras.zh: 它还为创造性的思考提供了契机。

paras.en: So, in your book, you talk about the importance of “deep play”.
paras.zh: 那么，您在书中谈到了“深度游戏”的重要性。

paras.en: Is that a recognised psychological concept?
paras.zh: 这是一个公认的心理学概念吗？

w.m: adj. 公认的；得到认可的

paras.en: The term deep play comes originally from Jeremy Bentham but a cultural anthropologist called Clifford Geertz popularised it.
paras.zh: 深度游戏这个说法最初来自杰里米·边沁，但让它流行起来的是一位名叫克利福德·格尔茨的文化人类学家。

paras.en: People who are really ambitious and think about their work an awful lot will have these hobbies that look like they absorb gigantic amounts of time and energy.
paras.zh: 那些雄心勃勃、花大量心思琢磨自己工作的人，往往会有这样一些爱好：看上去要占用海量的时间和精力。

w.m: adj. 有抱负的；雄心勃勃的
v. 占用，耗费（时间、精力）；吸收

paras.en: There are all kinds of different terms for roughly the same kind of thing, that is, serious leisure.
paras.zh: 有各种各样不同的说法，指的大致都是同一类东西，那就是严肃休闲。

paras.en: The fact that there is no one term for this activity reflects the fact that there is no clear idea of its importance.
paras.zh: 这种活动没有一个统一的叫法，这一事实反映出人们对它的重要性并没有清晰的认识。

paras.en: But what I came to see is that these kind of activities, like, for example, mountain climbing, have a deeper value that makes the investment of time and energy worthwhile.
paras.zh: 但我逐渐认识到，这类活动，比如登山，具有更深层的价值，让投入的时间和精力物有所值。

paras.en: Then what about sleep?
paras.zh: 那睡眠呢？

paras.en: If you don’t care about your mental development or your body, then forget about sleep.
paras.zh: 如果你不在乎自己的心智发展或身体，那睡眠就不用管了。

paras.en: Otherwise sleep is the original rest.
paras.zh: 否则的话，睡眠就是原初意义上的休息。

paras.en: Scientists still haven’t found the one thing that explains why if you have a nervous system you need to sleep, and even if you don’t have a nervous system you need to sleep—plants do something similar.
paras.zh: 科学家们至今还没有找到那个唯一能解释原因的东西：为什么有神经系统就需要睡眠，而就算没有神经系统也需要睡眠——植物也会做类似的事情。

paras.en: Sleep is incredibly important for brain maintenance.
paras.zh: 睡眠对大脑的维护极其重要。

paras.en: When we sleep the brain takes time to clear out plaques and toxins that have built up during the hours we are awake.
paras.zh: 我们睡觉的时候，大脑会花时间清除在我们醒着的那几个小时里积聚起来的斑块和毒素。

paras.en: Even though we’re not aware of it, sleep also helps us push forward on questions and problems we’re working on during our waking hours.
paras.zh: 尽管我们意识不到，但睡眠还能帮助我们在清醒时正在琢磨的疑问和难题上取得进展。

paras.en: What’s the most surprising insight or fact you came across in your research?
paras.zh: 您在研究中偶然发现的最令人惊讶的见解或事实是什么？

paras.en: The biggest thing that I took away from this book is it’s completely changed the way that I think about creativity.
paras.zh: 我从这本书里得到的最大收获是，它彻底改变了我对创造力的看法。

paras.en: I used to have a romantic notion in the 19th-century sense that creativity was something that was irrational and chaotic, that proceeds from a bolt from the blue, where you get inspired and then start working.
paras.zh: 我过去抱有一种19世纪意义上的浪漫观念，认为创造力是一种非理性的、混乱的东西，源于突如其来的灵光一现：你受到启发，然后才开始工作。

w.m: adj. 浪漫的；浪漫主义的
突如其来的事；意外之事

paras.en: And what you see in lots of creative lives is a completely different model of working.
paras.zh: 而在许多有创造力的人的人生中，你看到的是一种完全不同的工作模式。

w.m: adj. 有创造力的；创造性的

paras.en: As the saying goes: “Inspiration exists but it has to find you at work.”
paras.zh: 正如俗话所说：“灵感是存在的，但它必须在你工作时找到你。”

paras.en: People who have long creative lives, who do really great work for decades, they don’t get inspired and start work.
paras.zh: 那些创作生涯很长、几十年来一直做着真正出色工作的人，并不是先获得灵感再开始工作。

paras.en: They start work and get inspired.
paras.zh: 他们是先开始工作，然后才获得灵感。

paras.en: And they do this every day.
paras.zh: 而且他们每天都这样做。

paras.en: That was a real revelation.
paras.zh: 那真是一个启示。

paras.en: OK, thank you very much, Allen, for joining us tonight.
paras.zh: 好的，艾伦，非常感谢你今晚来参加我们的节目。

paras.en: Pleasure.
paras.zh: 我的荣幸。

paras.en: This is the end of Part Two of the interview.
paras.zh: 访谈的第二部分到此结束。

paras.en: Questions 6 to 10 are based on what you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第6至10题基于你刚才听到的内容。

paras.en: Question 6: What is the man’s definition of rest?
paras.zh: 第6题：这位男士对休息的定义是什么？

paras.en: Question 7: Which activity has a deeper value for worthwhile investment of time and energy?
paras.zh: 第7题：哪项活动具有更深层的价值，值得投入时间和精力？

paras.en: Question 8: What is the function of sleep, according to the man?
paras.zh: 第8题：根据这位男士的说法，睡眠的作用是什么？

paras.en: Question 9: What is the man’s most surprising insight from his research?
paras.zh: 第9题：这位男士在研究中最令人惊讶的见解是什么？

paras.en: Question 10: What is the main topic of the interview?
paras.zh: 第10题：这次访谈的主要话题是什么？

paras.en: This is the end of Section B, Interview.
paras.zh: B节“访谈”到此结束。

paras.en: This is the end of Part One, Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第一部分“听力理解”到此结束。
